run.description:
Run JavaScript that drives tabs with the same tools, several steps in one call: loops over pages, forms filled in a go, a list scrolled until a row shows. Each method is the tool of the same name and goes through the same checks (Send, Pay and the like still wait for the user). Synchronous (await is fine and does nothing). Print with console.log; the value you return is printed too. A failed step throws with the tool's message.
  const t = open(url)            // or tab(id), tabs()
  t.snapshot({interactive})      // text; t.refs(/Invite/) → [{ref, line}], t.find('Save') → ref or null
  t.locate(['Email', 'Save'])    // one look, every name at once: {Email: 'e4', Save: null}
  t.eval(js) t.upload(ref, paths) t.download(ref)
  open(url).opened is the page's first snapshot; tab() with no id is the tab last opened
  t.click(ref) t.click({x, y}) t.type(ref, text, {submit}) t.type(text) t.choose(ref, value)
  t.press(keys) t.hover(ref) t.drag(ref, toRef) t.drag(ref, {dx, dy}) t.drag({x, y}, {x, y}) t.scroll(ref|null, dy)
  t.dialog(accept, text) t.text() t.wait(forText) t.navigate(url) t.fetch(url) t.show() t.close()
  sleep(ms), keep (an object that lasts between runs)
Each action returns what changed on the page, as the tool does. At most 200 steps a run.
outputLimit bounds printed text (8000 characters by default, 256–32000); print only the result you need.
A promise that remains pending is an error; there are no background JavaScript tasks here.

watch.description: Watch a thread for someone's reply: every two hours for `days` (default 3), Pane quietly checks it and, when the reply comes, puts it on the user's new tab. Call it after you send something the user is waiting to hear back on, or when they ask to know about a reply. With stop and an id, ends a watch.

watch_page.description: Watch a page for the user until something on it holds: a price under a number, back in stock, an order shipped. Call it as soon as they ask to be told when that happens; never offer a routine for it. You write the check once: the body of a JavaScript function of (text, html, url, json, number) that returns { value, holds }, value what it read in words ("$189", "In stock"), holds true when the user's condition is met; return null when the page doesn't show the thing. text is the page's words, html its markup (JSON-LD and meta tags are there), json the body when it is JSON, number(s) the first number in a string ("$1,299.99" is 1299.99). No DOM, no network: work over the strings. Pane reads the page itself every `every` minutes (30; 5 at least) with the space's sign-ins, runs the check with no model, and the moment it holds tells the user with `tell` ("{value}" is what it read) and ends the watch; the tab's row says "Watching: " and until. The check is tried on the page at once: an error comes back to fix, and if it holds already no watch is set. With watch and check: a watch's check written again. With stop (a watch's id, or all): ended. With nothing: the watches set.
